For the officer joining this caseload, here is a concise orientation note:  

**Case Distribution**: Cases are concentrated in **فیصل آباد** (Faisalabad: 19 cases), **لاہور** (Lahore: 18 cases), and **راولپنڈی** (Rawalpindi: 10 cases). Other districts, including **اسلام آباد** (Islamabad), **چنیوٹ** (Chiniot), **حیدر آباد** (Hyderabad), **کراچی ایسٹ** (Karachi East), **کراچی وسطی** (Karachi Central), and **ملتان** (Multan), have 5–1 cases each [Document 1].  

**Case Mix**: Current cases (2026) show a **surge in Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)** cases (39) compared to 2024 (13), alongside a decline in **Arms Ordinance 1965** cases (16 vs. 13). New categories include **CNSA 1997** (12), **PECA 2016** (9), **Punjab Domestic Violence Act** (4), and **Illegal Dispossession Act 2005** (2), reflecting diversification into domestic violence, economic crimes, and land disputes [Document 2].  

**Arrests**: Only **11 of 73 FIRs** record at least one arrest; **62 FIRs** note no arrests (due to ongoing investigations, absconding, or explicit non-arrest notes) [Document 3].  

**Reporting Delays**: The mean time from incident to report is **1401.3 minutes (~23.4 hours)** in 2026 (across 51 FIRs), a stark increase from **15.0 minutes** in 2024 [Document 4].  

**Weapon Licensing**: Of 32 weapon-register entries, **30 recovered weapons** have **no licence recorded**, and **2 entries** lack licence status entirely, leaving compliance unconfirmed [Document 5].  

Officers should prioritize districts with higher case volumes, prepare for low arrest rates, and note delays in reporting. Weapon-related cases under Arms Ordinance 1965 and PPC require attention to unlicensed weapons and evolving legal frameworks.
